slices.next: Deploy magna-carta-sign before the app worker (the SIGN_SERVICE binding blocks the app-worker deploy until the sign worker exists), then provision the platform seal identity with pnpm run platform-seal-certificate; after that, timestamp/LTV levels behind a TSA, independent-validator (pyHanko/DSS) conformance, cross-reference-stream originals in the seal primitive (classic tables only today), and the consumer/UI surfaces.
slices.notes: The pure-Rust PDF **engine** substrate is built (see _PDF render engine_, cross-cutting). E-signature core substantially built (Opus 4.8), end to end and proven: the PAdES **seal primitive** in `pdf-core` (prefix-preserving incremental update + exact `/ByteRange` + reserved `/Contents` + CMS splice) with **WASM bindings** and the real `@magna-carta/pdf` `createSealEngine` adapter; the **CMS backend** (`@magna-carta/signing`, pkijs/WebCrypto, key host-side) now at **PAdES-B-B baseline** with ESS **signing-certificate-v2**; the `SealEngine` port + `sealDocument` orchestrator; the ESIGN/UETA model + **Certificate of Completion** (assemble + render). The seal now has a **home and a door**: the dedicated **`sign-worker`** (`magna-carta-sign`) runs the engine + CMS in-process and holds the platform signing key (proven on workerd — it seals a real PDF and verifies the embedded CMS), and the app worker exposes **`POST /api/v1/documents/seal`** (permission `esign:seal`, chokepoint, redacted `esign.sealed` audit) forwarding to it over a `SIGN_SERVICE` binding through a reusable `SealPort` adapter, with deferred-activation `503` until the signing identity is set. An **e2e test** drives a real PDF prepare→sign→embed and verifies the seal (node + workerd); the route is covered end to end (chokepoint, sealed shape, server-set signing-time/observed-IP, not-configured `503`). **Provisioning is a single command**: `pnpm run platform-seal-certificate` mints the RSA-3072 key + self-signed document-signing certificate (correct `keyUsage`/EKU/SKI/serial/RDN encoding, verified independently by openssl) and prints the two `wrangler secret put` commands that activate the seal; the generator is a tested library function whose test proves the exported key re-imports and seals. Runbook: _E-signature seal Worker_ in [`operations.md`](docs/conventions/operations.md). Remaining: timestamp/LTV levels (B-T/B-LT/B-LTA, needs a TSA), independent-validator (pyHanko/DSS) conformance, and the consumer/UI surfaces.

Build slice 2·6·1 shipped: the walking slice, template registration through to a filed document.
`@magna-carta/document-assembly` is a pure package over `fflate` + `fast-xml-parser` (the
`@magna-carta/metadata` substrate) holding the guarded OOXML reader/writer, the macro stripper and its
independent re-verification gate, the normalization pass, the declarative merge-field dictionary and
its formatters, the batched resolution pipeline, and the substitution engine. Four per-firm tables
(`document_template`, immutable `document_template_version`, `document_template_field_mapping`,
`document_assembly`), nine catalogue routes plus submit/poll, a `DocumentAssemblyJob` Durable Object
over a dedicated queue, and the assembled document filed through `initiateUpload` /
`completeUploadSession` — the one ingest chokepoint, no bypass. Owner decisions taken: `{{key}}` is
the single stored placeholder form, and the merge is in-house rather than an adopted library.

Both registration transforms of the firm's own document are **opt-in and always reported**, revised
on 2026-08-04 evening. Converting Word merge fields runs only on request, and a template registered
without it keeps them — each recorded on the field manifest with the part it sits in and the frozen
cached text it will print, reported again by every assembly in the response and on the provenance row,
and landing the assembly on `succeeded_with_absences`, so a blank that does not look like a blank
meets the same absence model an ordinary missing value does. Removing macros likewise runs only on
request; a macro-bearing upload without the opt-in is refused with both remedies named, never stored
carrying live macros and never stripped silently. The per-firm **field-mapping library** behind
`MergeFieldNameResolver` is built: confirmed Word-name-to-key mappings written when a conversion
confirms them, read once per registration, listed and deletable under `templates:manage`.

Remaining for the subsystem: conditionals and repeats (2·6·2), PDF output and the signature hand-off
(2·6·3), authoring surfaces (2·6·4), the interface seams, and the load-profile volume profile.

slices.notes: `crates/ocr-core` (PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6, small tier, via `ort`/ONNX) + `containers/ocr` + `apps/ocr-worker`; `POST /api/v1/ocr`, `tools:ocr` permission. Page selection weighs visible-text coverage against raster coverage rather than glyph presence, so a Bates-stamped scan is still recognized; outsize pages are rastered to fit a pixel budget and geometry bombs refused. Page-walk, skip-gate, coordinate-transform, raster-cap, and wire-mapping logic are unit- and integration-tested green; model-backed recognition runs in the container CI job. UI deferred.

slices.next: Deferred seams — rotated-page (`/Rotate` 90/180/270) placement: the layer is written in the unrotated frame, so selection geometry is off on rotated scans (text stays searchable) — needs a counter-rotating text matrix like `bates.rs`; ingest-pipeline wiring (queues, per-job Durable Object, search index; blocked on the unbuilt discovery/search subsystem); skewed-quad placement beyond axis-aligned bounds; embedding a glyphless font if a target viewer needs a rendered selection glyph; and the UI. (The conversion orchestrator's scanned→searchable edge is now wired — `pdf → searchable-pdf` in the conversion registry, dispatched to the OCR service. An adversarial review hardened the writer: non-BMP characters, font-name collisions, and degenerate word boxes are fixed.)
slices.notes: `pdf_core::write_searchable_text_layer` writes an invisible (`3 Tr`) OCR text layer over a scanned page — selectable, copyable, searchable, with no visible change — reusing the Bates additive-append rule (existing bytes untouched, one shared non-embedded Type0/Identity-H font + ToUnicode, byte-identical output; Latin/CJK/Greek covered). Reachable end to end: the OCR container serves `POST /ocr/searchable` (PDF in, searchable PDF out, owning the line-text/word-box split), the ocr-worker proxies it, and the main worker exposes `POST /api/v1/ocr/searchable` behind `tools:ocr`, streaming the PDF back. A pdf-eval operation checks the additive-only invariant. UI and ingest/orchestrator dispatch deferred.

slices.next: Deploy-gated — `apps/search-worker` (the always-warm Container that range-reads splits from R2 and serves `/index`, `/query`, `/remove`) is the only thing between the parked `deferred` jobs and real hits; the adapter already calls exactly those endpoints, so deploying it needs no code change here. Then the semantic half (Vectorize namespace-per-firm through `InferencePort.embed`; the RRF that fuses it is done), the matter-scoped `/api/v1` route behind a `discovery:search` permission plus its UI (built after the engine, so the route never ships returning engine-not-implemented), and compaction (merge the small per-document splits, swap the catalog). One known extract gap: a born-digital PDF's existing text layer is not read back out — the recognition engine skips such pages — so it records `unextractable` rather than indexing empty; closing it needs `crates/pdf-core`'s `page_text_glyphs` exposed through `packages/pdf`, behind the same `TextExtractionPort`.
slices.notes: Tantivy keyword search over immutable per-firm splits in R2 — a split is a self-contained segment bundle plus a footer, so a query prunes on footers and range-reads only the postings it walks, making per-query I/O scale with query selectivity rather than corpus size. Built: the pure-Rust engine core (`crates/search-core`, a read-only `Directory` over a `RangeReader`), the per-firm `index_split` catalog and its data-access statements, the `SearchIndexPort` with typed outcomes, keyword/hybrid query composition with reciprocal rank fusion, and the **write pipeline** — a `SearchIndexJob` Durable Object over a dead-lettered queue that turns each committed document version into one split at a derived, content-addressed key, so a retry converges instead of duplicating. Gated per firm by `search.indexing_enabled` (off by default) and enqueued off the clean ingest commit. Wired-but-dormant in the conversion subsystem's sense: with no engine deployed, a job parks in a distinct `deferred` state — acked and re-startable, never retried into a dead-letter — so deploying the engine drains the backlog naturally and no document is silently dropped meanwhile.
